name: Water Court
summary: A single-tower mosque rests above one broad water ribbon, evoking the stillness of a courtyard pool.
why: The dome and its doorway share x=55. The minaret connects directly to the hall through an attached wing and every architectural foot meets y=65. A generous open gap separates the flowing pool from the solid building, and the same sea-glass color joins the visual language.
risk: The water association is emotional rather than a literal prayer-time symbol. At 24 pixels it remains a simple mosque with a quiet base wave.
reasonToChoose: You want a calm mosque with clear, connected architecture and a gentle sense of depth.
